steps.title: Accounts & access
steps.goal: Every third-party account the build needs exists under one founder email with 2FA on, before any agent needs a key: GitHub (repo default branch main, Actions on, Claude connector with write access), Supabase (organization on the Free plan, no project yet), Vercel (team on Pro with the GitHub App installed for ChurchAppCLD, no project yet), Stripe (test mode), plus Expo and a Google account for Firebase (may be deferred to step 4.5) and optionally a domain and a Resend account. The Anacast identity decisions the code depends on — Android package id (recommended `com.anacast.app`), deep-link scheme `anacast`, brand colours, production domain — are confirmed or explicitly deferred and recorded in HANDOFF.md, and a password-manager vault exists so no secret ever lands in git, a prompt, or chat.
steps.founder_checklist:
## 0.1 — Accounts & access (founder, about 60 minutes, no code)

Use one email for everything below (`<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`) and turn on two-factor authentication on every account — these accounts will hold church members' personal data.

1. **GitHub — repository `RadioDinner/ChurchAppCLD` (already exists).**
   1. github.com → `RadioDinner/ChurchAppCLD` → Settings → General → "Default branch" = `main` (change it if it still points at a `claude/...` branch).
   2. Settings → Branches: no protection rule on `main` (agents push to `main` directly — standing order 6).
   3. Settings → Actions → General → "Allow all actions and reusable workflows" (step 1.1 adds one non-blocking CI workflow).
   4. claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → GitHub: confirm the Claude GitHub App has read/write access to `ChurchAppCLD`.
2. **Supabase account (Free plan).**
   1. supabase.com → "Start your project" → sign in with GitHub or `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`.
   2. Create an Organization: name `Anacast`, plan **Free** (founder decision 10).
   3. Do **not** create a project yet — step 2.4 creates it (US East) once `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` exists. A Free project pauses after 7 idle days; creating it early only burns that window.
3. **Vercel account + team on Pro.**
   1. vercel.com → "Continue with GitHub" (the GitHub identity that owns `RadioDinner`).
   2. Dashboard → team switcher (top-left) → "Create Team" → name `Anacast` → plan **Pro** (US$20 per member per month; founder decision 10: "Vercel PRO at launch"). Be on Pro before step 2.5: the repo ships `apps/web/vercel.json` with a `*/5 * * * *` cron, which a Hobby deployment rejects, and Hobby forbids commercial use.
   3. Team Settings → Git → "Connect" GitHub → install the Vercel GitHub App on the `RadioDinner` account → "Only select repositories" → `ChurchAppCLD`.
   4. Do **not** import a project yet (step 2.5).
4. **Stripe account (test mode).**
   1. dashboard.stripe.com/register → `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` → business name `Anacast` (editable later) → verify the email.
   2. Stay in **Test mode** (toggle top-right / "Sandboxes"). Do not activate live payments until launch; the product, the US$50/month price and the webhook are created in step 3.9.
5. **Expo account (needed at step 4.5 — may be created then).** expo.dev/signup → `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` → username `anacast` (or similar). The free plan is enough for EAS Build (monthly build quota, lower-priority queue).
6. **Google account for Firebase (needed at step 4.5 — may be created then).** Decide which Google account will own the Firebase project (console.firebase.google.com) and, later, the Google Play Console developer account (US$25 one-time; identity verification can take days — needed only for a Play Store listing, not for the sideloaded APK of Checkpoint C).
7. **Optional now, needed by step 3.9 at the latest: domain and Resend.**
   1. If you want a custom domain (for example `app.anacast.<tld>`), register it now. Until then `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is the Vercel URL `https://<project>.vercel.app`. Changing the domain later changes invite/share URLs and the Supabase redirect URLs; share links already issued keep the old host.
   2. resend.com → account with `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` (free tier: 3,000 emails/month). Sending from your own address requires a verified domain, so Resend is only useful once the domain exists. Without it the app shows invite links for copy/paste and Supabase's rate-limited default SMTP sends the OTP codes.
8. **Identity decisions (record each one).**
   1. Android package id: you gave `com.Anacast.app`. **Recommended: `com.anacast.app`** (all lowercase — uppercase segments are legal for Android but conflict with Java package conventions and some tooling). It cannot change after the first Play upload. Confirm one value.
   2. Deep-link scheme: `anacast` (replaces the plan's `churchapp` placeholder). Confirm.
   3. App display name: `Anacast` (given).
   4. Brand colours: a primary colour as a hex code (optionally an accent). "Deferred" is acceptable — web and mobile use a neutral default theme until you supply them.
   5. Production domain: the domain from 7.1, or "deferred (Vercel URL)".
9. **Password manager.** Create a vault or folder "Anacast — infrastructure" with entries for GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, Stripe, Expo, Google, registrar/Resend. Every key produced in steps 2.4, 2.5, 3.9 and 4.5 goes there. Never paste a key into git, into a Claude Code prompt (`prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim), or into chat.
10. **Record in `HANDOFF.md`.** Under "Environment status" add a line per account (done, or deferred to the step that needs it); under "Decisions" add the package id, scheme, brand colours (or deferred) and domain (or deferred). Either edit the file yourself and commit, or paste the helper prompt below into a Claude Code session with your values filled in.
steps.helper_prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is the helper for step 0.1 "Accounts & access" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `HANDOFF.md` and `docs/PLAN.md` §13 before editing. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
Record the outcome of my account set-up and identity decisions in `HANDOFF.md`. No code; no files other than `HANDOFF.md`, `docs/TODO.md` and the session log.

## Inputs (ask me for any value that is missing instead of guessing)
- Accounts: GitHub done; Supabase organization (Free) done; Vercel team (Pro) done; Stripe (test mode) done; Expo <done | deferred to 4.5>; Google/Firebase <done | deferred to 4.5>; domain <value | deferred>; Resend <done | deferred to 3.9>.
- Android package id: <com.anacast.app | com.Anacast.app>
- Deep-link scheme: <anacast>
- Brand colours: <#RRGGBB primary, optional accent | deferred>
- Production domain: <domain | deferred (Vercel URL)>

## Build
1. `HANDOFF.md` → "Environment status": insert a first item "0. Accounts (step 0.1)" listing each account as done or deferred (with the step that needs it). Leave the other numbered items as they are.
2. "Decisions (do not re-open without the founder)": add app display name `Anacast`; the Android package id exactly as I gave it (if it is not all-lowercase, add "lowercase `com.anacast.app` recommended; cannot change after the first Play upload"); the deep-link scheme; brand colours or "deferred — neutral default theme"; production domain or "deferred — `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` = Vercel URL".
3. "Open questions for the founder": remove the parts of question 9 that are now answered; keep whatever is deferred.
4. Update the "_Last updated_" line.

## Constraints
- Do not write any email address, password, key or token into the repo.
- Do not create code, packages, scripts or migrations. Do not edit `new_session_instructions.md`.

## Verify
- `git diff HANDOFF.md` shows only the additions above and contains no secret.

## Finish
Tick step 0.1 in `docs/TODO.md`, write `session_log.md`, commit `docs: record founder accounts and identity decisions (step 0.1)`, push `main`. If a value I gave contradicts the plan (for example a package id that is not lowercase), record it verbatim and note the recommendation — do not silently change it.
done_when: GitHub: `main` is the default branch of RadioDinner/ChurchAppCLD, there is no branch-protection rule on it, Actions are enabled, and the Claude GitHub connector has write access to the repository.
Supabase: you can sign in; an organization named Anacast on the Free plan exists; no project has been created yet (step 2.4 creates it).
Vercel: a team on the Pro plan exists; the Vercel GitHub App is installed with access to ChurchAppCLD; no project has been imported yet (step 2.5 imports it).
Stripe: the test-mode dashboard loads under your account; live payments are not activated.
Expo and Google/Firebase accounts exist, or HANDOFF.md says they are deferred to step 4.5.

HANDOFF.md records the Android package id (recommended `com.anacast.app`; the given `com.Anacast.app` recorded verbatim if kept), deep-link scheme `anacast`, display name Anacast, and either a value or 'deferred' for brand colours and production domain.
A password-manager vault for the project exists and no secret has been written into the repo, a Claude Code prompt, or chat.
Two-factor authentication is on for GitHub, Supabase, Vercel and Stripe.

steps.title: Monorepo scaffold
steps.goal: The repository becomes a working pnpm 10 + Turborepo 2 workspace with three empty but lint/typecheck/test-clean TypeScript packages (`@church/domain`, `@church/db`, `@church/supabase-client`), shared `@church/tsconfig` and `@church/eslint-config` tooling packages, root config (package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml with hoisted linker + onlyBuiltDependencies + catalog, turbo.json, tsconfig.base.json, .nvmrc, prettier, editorconfig, .env.example), a committed lockfile, a non-blocking GitHub Actions workflow whose later-phase steps are file-guarded, `apps/web/vercel.json` with the Pro `*/5 * * * *` cron, `docs/ENV.md` covering every environment variable including `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB`, and an updated README. `pnpm install && pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` is green from a fresh clone; no app code, migrations, Next.js or Expo yet.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 1.1 "Monorepo scaffold" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §2–§3, §7 (env var list) and §10 step 2, and `docs/DESIGN.md` §2–§3, §8 (env vars paragraph), §11 Phase 1 step 2 and §12 before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, the repository is a working pnpm 10 + Turborepo 2 workspace: three empty but lint/typecheck/test-clean TypeScript packages (`@church/domain`, `@church/db`, `@church/supabase-client`), two shared tooling packages (`@church/tsconfig`, `@church/eslint-config`), the root config files, a committed `pnpm-lock.yaml`, a non-blocking GitHub Actions workflow, `apps/web/vercel.json` with the Vercel Pro cron schedule, and `docs/ENV.md` describing every environment variable the project will ever need. From a fresh clone on Node 22, `pnpm install && pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` is green. There is still no application code, no migration, no Next.js app and no Expo app.

## Inputs / prior state
- The repo contains only docs and session conventions: `CLAUDE.md`, `new_session_instructions.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/PLAN.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `docs/TODO.md`, `scripts/session/new-session.sh`, `Session log/`. Nothing exists under `apps/`, `packages/`, `tooling/`, `supabase/`.
- A premature scaffold was committed and reverted in session 001 (`git show 7db4f3f --stat`). You may look at it for reference, but its `apps/mobile/package.json` with hand-pinned Expo versions is exactly what the standing orders forbid — do not resurrect the apps.
- Tools: Node 22 (`node -v`), pnpm 10 (`pnpm -v`). No Docker. Step 0.1 (founder accounts) may or may not be done; nothing here depends on it.

## Build
1. Root `package.json`: `"name": "churchappcld"`, `"private": true`, `"packageManager": "pnpm@<exact version from pnpm -v>"`, `"engines": {"node": ">=22"}`. Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` → `turbo run <task>`; `format` → `prettier --write .`, `format:check` → `prettier --check .`; `db:up` → `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh`, `db:apply` → `bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh`, `db:test` → `bash scripts/db/test.sh`, `db:types` → `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh`, `db:check` → `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh`, `session:new` → `bash scripts/session/new-session.sh`. The `scripts/db/*` files arrive in step 1.2; declaring the scripts now is intended. devDependencies: `turbo` 2.10.12, `prettier` 3.9.6, `typescript` `catalog:`.
2. `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: `packages: [apps/*, packages/*, tooling/*]`; `nodeLinker: hoisted` (single node_modules tree — required by Metro later; this is the only place the setting lives, do NOT add an `.npmrc`); `onlyBuiltDependencies: [esbuild, "@swc/core", sharp, unrs-resolver, "@tailwindcss/oxide", protobufjs, core-js]`, extended after install from any "Ignored build scripts" warning; `catalog:` holding ONLY deps shared by web and mobile that `expo install` does not manage: `react` 19.2.3 and `react-dom` 19.2.3 (exact — Expo SDK 57 pin), `@types/react` on the 19.2 line matching React 19.2 (check `npm view @types/react version`; DESIGN §3 says `~19.1`, treat that as stale and record the value you used in HANDOFF version pins), `typescript` ~5.9.3, `zod` 4.5.4, `@supabase/supabase-js` 2.112.4, `@tanstack/react-query` 5.102.8, `date-fns` 4.4.0, `@date-fns/tz` (current 1.x). No `expo-*`, `react-native-*` or `next` in the catalog — ever.
3. `turbo.json`: `$schema`, `globalDependencies: ["tsconfig.base.json", "pnpm-workspace.yaml"]`, tasks `build` (`dependsOn: ["^build"]`, outputs `.next/**`, `!.next/cache/**`, `dist/**`, `env`: `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, `SUPABASE_*`, `STRIPE_*`, `RESEND_*`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`, `CRON_SECRET`, `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET`), `dev` (`cache: false`, `persistent: true`), `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`.
4. `tsconfig.base.json` (repo root — the single source of compiler options): `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `esModuleInterop`, `skipLibCheck`, `resolveJsonModule`, `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames`, `module: esnext`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, `target: es2022`, `lib: [es2023]`.
5. `.nvmrc` = `22`. `.prettierrc` (semi, singleQuote, printWidth 110, trailingComma all). `.prettierignore` (node_modules, .next, .turbo, .expo, dist, build, coverage, pnpm-lock.yaml, `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`, `Session log`, .local-pg). `.editorconfig` (utf-8, lf, 2-space indent, final newline; no trailing-whitespace trim for `*.md`). Leave `.gitignore` unchanged unless a new artefact needs ignoring (it already covers `.env*`, `!.env.example`, `google-services.json`, `.turbo/`, `.vercel/`, `.local-pg/`).
6. `tooling/tsconfig/`: `package.json` (`"name": "@church/tsconfig"`, private, `"files": ["*.json"]`, no `exports` field so `"extends": "@church/tsconfig/library.json"` resolves through node_modules), `base.json` (extends `../../tsconfig.base.json`), `library.json` (extends `./base.json`; `noEmit`, `types: ["node"]`), `nextjs.json` (lib `dom`, `dom.iterable`, `es2023`; `jsx: preserve`; `allowJs`; `incremental`; `plugins: [{"name": "next"}]`), `react-native.json` (`jsx: react-jsx`; `types: ["react-native"]`). `nextjs.json` and `react-native.json` are consumed in steps 2.1 and 4.1.
7. `tooling/eslint-config/`: `package.json` (`"name": "@church/eslint-config"`, private, `"type": "module"`, exports `./base` → `./base.js`, `./next` → `./next.js`, `./expo` → `./expo.js`; dependencies `@eslint/js` 9.x, `typescript-eslint` 8.x, `eslint-config-prettier`, `globals`, `eslint-config-next` 16.3.4, `eslint-config-expo` 57.0.2; peerDependency `eslint ^9`), `base.js` (flat config: ignores for node_modules/dist/.next/.expo/coverage/*.d.ts; `js.configs.recommended`; `tseslint.configs.recommended`; `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` with inline type imports; `no-unused-vars` ignoring `^_`; `eslint-config-prettier` last), `next.js` (base + `eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals` + `eslint-config-next/typescript`), `expo.js` (base + `eslint-config-expo/flat`). ESLint 9 only — not 10 (`eslint-config-expo` is unvalidated on 10).
8. Packages. For each of `packages/domain` (`@church/domain`), `packages/db` (`@church/db`), `packages/supabase-client` (`@church/supabase-client`) create:
   - `package.json`: private, `"type": "module"`, `"exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"}` (TS source, no build step; Next uses `transpilePackages`, Metro resolves exports natively); scripts `lint: eslint .`, `typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.json`, and `test: vitest run` for domain and db (supabase-client has no test script yet). dependencies: domain → `zod: catalog:`; db → `@church/domain: workspace:*`, `@supabase/supabase-js: catalog:`; supabase-client → `@church/db: workspace:*`, `@supabase/supabase-js: catalog:`. devDependencies: `@church/eslint-config: workspace:*`, `@church/tsconfig: workspace:*`, `eslint` 9.x, `typescript: catalog:`, `@types/node` 22.x, `vitest` 4.1.x where there is a test script.
   - `tsconfig.json`: `{"extends": "@church/tsconfig/library.json", "include": ["src", "vitest.config.ts"]}`.
   - `eslint.config.js`: `import base from '@church/eslint-config/base'; export default base;`.
   - `src/index.ts`: one named placeholder export, e.g. `export const PACKAGE_NAME = '@church/domain' as const;` — steps 1.6/1.7 replace it.
   - For domain and db only: `vitest.config.ts` and `src/index.test.ts` asserting the placeholder, so `vitest run` executes at least one test (Vitest exits non-zero with zero test files).
9. Apps placeholders: `apps/web/README.md` and `apps/mobile/README.md`, three lines each — what will live there, which TODO step creates it (2.1 for web, 4.1 for mobile), and for mobile the rule "native dependency versions come only from `npx expo install`". NO `package.json` in either directory (pnpm ignores workspace directories without one), so nothing from Next or Expo is installed in this step.
10. `apps/web/vercel.json`: `{"$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json", "crons": [{"path": "/api/cron/tick", "schedule": "*/5 * * * *"}]}`. Founder decision 10: "Vercel Pro → cron `*/5 * * * *` allowed; `vercel.json` ships the Pro schedule (founder is on Pro) with the Hobby fallback documented." JSON carries no comments, so document the Hobby fallback (`0 12 * * *`) in `docs/ENV.md` and README. Location: DESIGN §2 draws `vercel.json` at the repo root, but Vercel reads `vercel.json` from the project's Root Directory, which will be `apps/web` (step 2.5). Put it at `apps/web/vercel.json`, describe the Vercel settings in `docs/ENV.md` (Root Directory `apps/web`, Framework Next.js, Node 22; Vercel detects the pnpm workspace and installs from the repo root), and record the deviation in HANDOFF.md under a new "Deviations from plan" heading.
11. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: one job `checks` on `push` to `main` and `pull_request`; `continue-on-error: true` (the workflow is informational, never blocking); `concurrency` with cancel-in-progress. Steps: `actions/checkout@v4`; `pnpm/action-setup@v4` with no version (it reads `packageManager`); `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: 22` and `cache: pnpm`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`. Then steps guarded with `if: hashFiles('<file>') != ''` so they switch on as later steps land: DB re-runnability + RLS tests (guard `scripts/db/test.sh`; add a `postgres:16` service container; step 1.2 owns what the scripts do in CI), web build (guard `apps/web/package.json`; run `pnpm --filter ./apps/web build` — a directory filter, so the package name chosen in 2.1 does not matter — with mock env `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_ci_placeholder`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000`), mobile checks (guard `apps/mobile/package.json`; `npx expo-doctor` then `npx expo export --platform android` in `apps/mobile`), types drift (guard `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`; run `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh` then `git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts`). With only the first five steps active, the workflow must pass today.
12. `.env.example` (root master template; `apps/web/.env.example` and `apps/mobile/.env.example` come in 2.1/4.1): every variable from `docs/ENV.md` with a placeholder value, grouped Supabase (web) / App / Upload cap / Stripe / Email / Mobile / EAS / Local database / E2E, one comment line per group saying which file it is copied to.
13. `docs/ENV.md`: one table per group with columns: variable | used by (web server, web browser, mobile, EAS, scripts, CI) | where it lives (Vercel env Production+Preview, EAS env, local `apps/web/.env.local` or `apps/mobile/.env`) | who fills it and in which TODO step | example or mock value | notes. Variables, names verbatim from DESIGN §8 and PLAN §7: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`; `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` (legacy alias `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, code reads either); `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` (legacy alias `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`; server only, never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, never in mobile); `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (optional, hosted typegen); `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`; `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` (default `50` — founder decision 10: Supabase Free caps each upload at 50 MB; the web upload UI reads this value and maps the storage "exceeds plan limit" error to a clear message; raise it together with the `sermon-media` bucket `file_size_limit` when the project moves to Pro); `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET` (`openssl rand -base64 32`); `CRON_SECRET`; `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`; `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` (the US$50/month recurring price, step 3.9); `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM` (optional — invite links are shown for copy/paste when absent); `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN` (optional, push); `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`; `EAS_PROJECT_ID`; `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` (an EAS *file* environment variable pointing at the gitignored `google-services.json`); `DATABASE_URL` (`postgresql://churchapp_owner@localhost:5432/churchapp?sslmode=disable`, or the fallback port printed by `scripts/db/local-up.sh`); Playwright mock values (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321`, dummy publishable key); `E2E_SUPABASE_URL`, `E2E_SUPABASE_KEY`, `E2E_SUPER_EMAIL`, `E2E_SUPER_PASSWORD`. Add three short sections: "Vercel project settings" (Root Directory `apps/web`, Node 22, Framework Next.js, cron Pro `*/5 * * * *`, Hobby fallback `0 12 * * *` and why Pro is required), "Where secrets live" (password manager only; never in git; never in a prompt — `prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim), "Supabase Free plan" (50 MB uploads, 1 GB storage, 500 MB DB, 5 GB egress, project pauses after 7 idle days and must be restored from the dashboard).
14. `README.md`: replace the stub with a one-paragraph description, prerequisites (Node 22 via `.nvmrc`, pnpm 10 via `corepack enable`), `pnpm install`, `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, the repo map from CLAUDE.md, the Vercel cron note, and pointers to `docs/TODO.md`, `docs/PLAN.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `docs/ENV.md`, `HANDOFF.md`. Keep the existing sentence about sessions and `new_session_instructions.md`.
15. Run `pnpm install`. Add each package named in an "Ignored build scripts" warning to `onlyBuiltDependencies` and re-run until the warning disappears. Commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Constraints
- Version pins from DESIGN §3 are ceilings on majors: TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Turbo 2.10, Vitest 4.1, Prettier 3.9, Zod 4.5, supabase-js 2.112, React 19.2.3 exact. Use `npm view <pkg> version` only to confirm a version exists; never bump a major.
- Do not create `apps/web/package.json`, `apps/mobile/package.json`, `supabase/`, `scripts/db/`, or any migration. Do not add `expo-*`, `react-native-*` or `next` anywhere. Do not run `npx create-next-app` or `npx create-expo-app`.
- No `.npmrc` (settings live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`). No build step for packages (TS source exports). No `postinstall` scripts.
- Never `supabase db push`. Do not edit `new_session_instructions.md`. No model identifiers in commits or files. No secrets anywhere; `.env.example` holds placeholders only.
- If the npm registry is only reachable through a proxy, fix the proxy configuration; never disable TLS verification.

## Verify
- `node -v` → `v22.x`; `pnpm -v` → `10.x` and equals the `packageManager` field.
- `pnpm install` → completes with no "Ignored build scripts" warning.
